title: Wind Turbine Operational Analysis & Clustering
text:
← Back to Portfolio

Wind Turbine Operational Analysis & Clustering
Context: Data Analytics 344 · R-based Academic Project


The Problem

The objective was to discover patterns and groupings in unlabeled 10-minute aggregated sensor recordings from a wind turbine.
The raw dataset was highly complex, containing 60 different features with varying scales, outliers, and irregularities.



The Approach

Conducted exploratory data analysis, handled outliers, and generated Pearson correlation heatmaps to understand feature relationships.
Trained a 10x10 Self-Organizing Map (SOM) over 300 epochs to identify underlying patterns.
Used the SOM and a U-Matrix to reduce dimensionality, selecting 10 non-redundant, high-impact features (e.g., PitchAngle, RotorSpeed, Torque).
Evaluated cluster tendency, achieving a Hopkins Statistic of 1.
Applied K-Means clustering, determining the optimal number of clusters to be 3 via the Elbow Method and Silhouette scores.



The Outcome

Final project mark: 96%
Successfully segmented the turbine data into three distinct, cohesive operational clusters.
Demonstrated clear relationships between environmental inputs (wind speed) and mechanical responses.


Business Impact: These clusters can be utilised by site managers to identify abnormal mechanical stress and perform predictive maintenance before component failure, and to analyse correlations between components during high and low stress situations.

A 12-week academic simulation project replicating the management of a $380,000 warehouse automation initiative.

title: EasyEquities Portfolio Tracker
text:
← Back to Portfolio

EasyEquities Portfolio Tracker
Context: Personal Project · Python, C# .NET, & OCR
A custom desktop application that extracts portfolio data from screenshots and automates Excel historical reporting.


The Problem

Updating weekly portfolio performance required manually typing balances, profit/loss, and percentages from EasyEquities into Excel.
EasyEquities only provided current snapshots, making it difficult to track historical volatility, max drawdowns, or weekly returns over time.
Managing multiple accounts (Tax-Free, ZAR, USD) and comparing live strategies to demo accounts required clicking through isolated tabs.



The Approach

Application Architecture: Built a desktop interface that triggers a Python data processing script via command-line execution.
Data Extraction: Used Python’s easyocr library to extract raw text from uploaded screenshots of the portfolio.
Data Cleaning & Parsing: Wrote regular expressions (re) and coordinate-based logic (matching \(y\)-center and \(x\)-center bounding boxes) to reconstruct rows of financial data from unstructured image text.
Error Handling: Implemented mathematical cross-validation to fix common OCR mistakes. For example, catching dropped negative signs by verifying absolute values against percentage returns, and writing custom handlers for comma/decimal misreads.
Excel Integration: Used pandas and numpy to structure the cleaned data, and openpyxl to automatically overwrite and update the charts, tables, and heatmaps in the target Excel file.



The Outcome

Automated Workflow: Packaged the tool as a standalone .exe that takes a folder of screenshots as input and generates a fully updated Excel tracker with a single click.
Historical Tracking: The Excel file automatically calculates and charts weekly standard deviation (volatility), max drawdowns, and weekly return distributions for each individual holding.
Account Comparison: Built a feature to map and compare the performance of equivalent assets across live and demo accounts.
Currency Modeling: Added a scenario tool to calculate total ZAR-equivalent risk exposure based on manual USD/ZAR exchange rate adjustments.

← Back to Portfolio

LEAN Implementation & Buffer Optimization
Context: Vacation Training 351 (2024) · Dizani Consulting & Bravo Brands
A foundational industrial engineering internship focused on time studies, waste elimination, and physical layout redesign.


The Problem

The Bravo Lounge division manufactured 45,000 pieces of furniture a month but suffered from underutilized storage areas and inefficient material flow.
The factory had a long-term operational goal to create a First-In-First-Out (FIFO) buffer capable of holding two days’ worth of work (136 suites) spread across the bridge, the fibre department, and the foam cutting department.



The Approach

Conducted detailed time and motion studies in the foam cutting department to establish baseline standard times for the factory.
Analyzed the physical layout of the Fibre Department, identifying that racks were only being utilized on one side due to poor spatial orientation.
Executed a Phase 1 action plan to remove unused racks from the seaming department, replace them with sorting tables, and rotate the orientation of the remaining racks in the Fibre department to maximize accessibility.



The Outcome

Successfully reoriented the Fibre Department storage layout so both sides of the racks could be utilized, significantly increasing local storage capacity and ease of access.
This first-phase implementation successfully moved the factory closer to its overarching 136-suite buffer target before the project was formally handed over at the completion of the internship.
Earned a highly positive performance review, securing a return internship offer for the 2025 cycle.


Employer Testimonial: “Overall, Emmanuel was productive and enriching… His knowledge and skills acquired during this period will contribute positively to his academic and future career pursuits. Looking forward to round two!” - T. Els, Dizani Consulting

OEE Optimization & Digital Performance Tracking
Context: Vacation Training 451 (2025) · Dizani Consulting, Coricraft & Beekman Canopies
A high-impact process engineering internship focused on digitizing factory performance and driving Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE).


The Problem

Manufacturing plants at Coricraft and Beekman Canopies lacked real-time productivity tracking and suffered from unmeasured material flow bottlenecks.
The Beekman plant specifically needed a way to measure the critical laminating process output against target schedules.



The Approach

Coricraft: Set standard times for upholstery cells and integrated them into the Per4ma digital tracking system via a new barcode ticket system. Optimized CNC material yield using AlphaCam nesting software to group and cut wood parts with minimal waste.
Beekman Canopies: Conducted time studies for the laminating process, mathematically incorporating a 15% rest allowance to account for factory heat and paint fumes.
Proposed physical process improvements to eliminate idle time, including additional tool-washing basins and mechanical lifting levers to reduce dependency on unavailable manual labor.



The Outcome

Directly contributed to driving the Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE) at the Beekman plant from 72% to over 90%.
Enabled real-time, digital efficiency tracking for factory floor managers across multiple production lines.


Employer Testimonial: “This gentleman conducted himself to a level where Dizani will use him again and again. He did not just learn but contributed to the project at Beekman Canopies… Managed to take the team from 72% OEE into the 90% - Well done!!” - T. Els, Dizani Consulting

Supply Chain Strategy: The Fresh Connection
Context: Industrial Management 354 · Supply Chain Decision Simulation


The Problem

The objective was to turn around a failing fruit juice company from its demise over six successive simulation rounds.
The simulation required balancing severe trade-offs across four interconnected functions: Purchasing, Operations, Sales, and Supply Chain.
As the Purchasing lead, I was responsible for all decisions regarding suppliers and supplier agreements, directly impacting component availability and business profitability.



The Approach

Adopted a strict efficiency-focused strategy (as opposed to responsiveness) to ensure strategic fit and competitive alignment.
Analyzed round-over-round data to quantify the Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) for raw materials, successfully modeling how acquisition costs played a big role in total cost, in Orange especially.
Optimized component lot sizing and safety stock levels for critical materials (e.g., PET, Orange, Vitamin C) based on their specific product characteristics, volumes, and values.
Collaborated cross-functionally to ensure purchasing decisions did not negatively constrain warehousing capacity or cause production bottlenecks.



The Outcome

Final project mark: 80%, with a ROI of 38.31%.
Secured a 5th place overall finish in the cohort ranking of 28 teams.
Successfully aligned overarching business and supply chain strategies, translating them into tactical purchasing decisions.


Business Impact: Demonstrated the ability to practically apply a Sales and Operations Planning (S&OP) approach, proving that rigorous, data-driven supplier selection and TCO management directly drive higher Return on Investment (ROI).

title: Ergonomics & Thermal Stress Analysis
text:
← Back to Portfolio


Context: Industrial Ergonomics 414 · ECSA GA2 Project




Thermal stress in hot, humid work environments significantly impacts worker performance, safety, and health, leading to fatigue and reduced efficiency.
Because ambient conditions cannot always be fully eliminated (e.g., in mobile work contexts like Uber driving), mitigating heat stress requires a multidisciplinary engineering approach.
The objective was to apply scientific and engineering knowledge from first principles (ECSA GA2) to assess thermal risk and develop practical interventions.





Collected environmental data in a simulated hot/humid workspace (State A) and a cooler rest area (State B) using an RSPro IM-730 hygrometer.
Engineered a DIY black globe thermometer (placing the sensor inside a black cylindrical container) to accurately estimate radiant heat exposure.
Calculated the indoor Wet Bulb Globe Temperature (WBGT) to quantify the exact level of thermal strain.
Mapped the environmental data against ergonomic models (Niebel’s Work Design) for a worker producing 350 kcal/hr during seated, moderate arm work.





Peak measurements in the simulated workspace revealed a WBGT of 31.06°C.
Identified that this specific thermal load poses a high risk of heat stress, theoretically requiring a 75% rest allowance which severely limits productivity.
Recommended targeted interventions, including forced ventilation to enhance convective heat loss and strict, data-driven work-rest cycles.


Business Impact: Demonstrated the ability to physically measure, model, and mitigate environmental constraints that directly impact human operational efficiency and safety compliance.
